moc: Old St Paul's Cathedral: very long Gothic nave with a square crossing tower and NO spire (spire lost 1561), NO dome
Old London Bridge lined with houses
NO Wren dome or Wren steeples

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A thin needle spire rises on the skyline left of the big Gothic tower. The big tower has four corner pinnacles and sits on a short, low body. No very long nave is visible.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The skyline is meant to show Old St Paul's, which had a square crossing tower, a very long nave and no spire after 1561. The needle spire looks like a later spire or Wren-style steeple, and the short church body does not match Old St Paul's. This is a low-confidence reading.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A tall tower with a rounded, lantern-like top stands among the burning buildings on the right of the skyline.
ghi_chu.ly_do: It could be read as a Wren-style steeple. Wren's City steeples were built only after the Great Fire, from the 1670s onward. It is small and unclear, so this is a low-confidence reading.
